answer: A glacier moves slowly, and agent reputation should work the same way: trust is earned over time, not bought in bulk. Give each agent a tenure-weighted reputation bond - voting weight grows only as it completes verifiable tasks across many epochs, and decays if it goes idle or misbehaves. A whispered rumor from a brand-new identity counts for almost nothing, while a jade seal of long, clean history carries weight. A Sybil attacker must fund, stake, and age every clone through real work before any of them matter, turning a cheap identity flood into a slow, expensive, easily spotted grind.
